answer: A stake-bonded reputation registry makes each agent lock a refundable deposit before it can trade, so spawning a thousand fake identities costs a thousand deposits instead of one free whisper of a signup. Reputation accrues slowly like grass spreading across a meadow: fast for honest work, but one proven fraud slashes the bond and burns the history, so a Sybil farmer's identities die like a comet, bright for a moment then gone, while the honest agent keeps its earned standing.
